Wait—you knew it was from me and came anyway?

Three stubborn years... honestly, little brother, I missed you too.

meanings.note: Warm outer coat worn in cold or rainy weather.

examples.trans: The coat is here.

examples.text: Vemos los abrigos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the coats from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los abuelos also means 'grandparents'.

examples.trans: The grandfather is here.

examples.text: Vemos los abuelos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the grandfathers from the door.

meanings.note: Indefinite pronoun used in statements and questions.

examples.trans: Do you need anything else from the kitchen?

examples.text: Hay algo dentro de la caja.
examples.trans: There is something inside the box.

meanings.note: Refers exclusively to people.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de llamar a la puerta.
examples.trans: Someone just knocked at the door.
Is anyone at the front desk?

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Así que means 'so / therefore'.

examples.trans: Do it like this, slowly.
It is raining hard, so let us go inside.

meanings.note: Plural azules; azul marino means 'navy blue'.

examples.trans: It is a blue piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: Tener ... años expresses age; hace ... años means '... years ago'.

examples.trans: The year is here.

examples.text: Vemos los años desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the years from the door.

meanings.note: Tall, light home-baked cake popular for breakfast or afternoon merienda in Spain.

examples.trans: The sponge cake is here.

examples.text: Vemos los bizcochos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sponge cakes from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable in gender (el hermano cabezota / tres años cabezotas).

examples.trans: It is a stubborn piece.

examples.text: Tres años cabezotas... la verdad, hermanito, yo también te he echado de menos.
examples.trans: Three stubborn years... honestly, little brother, I missed you too.

meanings.note: Describes hot drinks, food, or water.

examples.trans: It is a hot piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene, señora: té caliente de menta con miel.
examples.trans: Here you are, madam: hot mint tea with honey.

meanings.note: De camino = on the way; todo el camino = all the way.

examples.trans: The way is here.

examples.text: Vemos los caminos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ways from the door.

meanings.note: Alto y claro = loud and clear; ¡Claro! / ¡Pues claro! = Of course!

examples.text: El mensaje es alto y claro.
examples.trans: The message is loud and clear.
Well of course you can come in!

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb with written accent.

examples.trans: What is your name?
How do I find the hardware shop?

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Detrás de + noun means 'behind something'.

examples.text: El jardín está detrás de la casa.
examples.trans: The garden is behind the house.

examples.text: Hay otra página detrás del aviso.
examples.trans: There is another page behind the notice.

meanings.note: Disculpe (usted) / Disculpa (tú) is polite 'excuse me'.

examples.trans: Excuse me, do you know what time it is?

examples.text: Nos disculpamos por el pequeño retraso.
examples.trans: We apologized for the brief delay.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

echar.gloss: to pour; to toss; to miss (echar de menos)

meanings.en: to pour; to toss; to miss (echar de menos)
meanings.note: Echar un vistazo = take a glance; echar de menos = miss someone.

examples.text: Echa un poco más de agua caliente.
examples.trans: Pour a little more hot water.

examples.text: Te he echado mucho de menos.
examples.trans: I have missed you very much.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Third-person feminine singular pronoun.

examples.text: Ella conoce muy bien esta calle.
examples.trans: She knows this street very well.
This gift is for her.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Standard word in Spain for feeling angry or upset with someone.

examples.trans: It is an angry piece.

examples.text: Suave, educada, de unos treinta y cinco años. Sonaba nervioso, no enfadado.
examples.trans: Soft, polite, around thirty-five. He sounded nervous, not angry.

meanings.note: Esconderse detrás de = to hide behind.

examples.text: Escondo el regalo en el armario.
examples.trans: I hide the present in the wardrobe.

examples.text: El gato se escondió detrás de la maceta.
examples.trans: The cat hid behind the flowerpot.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.
We hope you rest very well.

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.
This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Gracias por + noun/infinitive expresses 'thank you for...'.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your help!
Thank you for coming today.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.
We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Affectionate diminutive of hermano.

examples.trans: The little brother is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hermanitos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the little brothers from the door.

meanings.note: Universal friendly greeting at any hour of the day.

examples.trans: Hello, come in and sit down!
Hi, how are you doing today?

meanings.note: El día de hoy = today.

examples.trans: Today is finally Friday.
What are we having for breakfast today?

meanings.note: Polite reply meaning 'likewise / same to you', or 'anyway'.

examples.trans: 'Have a nice weekend!' 'Likewise!'

examples.text: Sabía quién era y vino igualmente.
examples.trans: He knew who it was and came anyway.

imprenta.gloss: printing press; block capitals (letra de imprenta)

meanings.en: printing press; block capitals (letra de imprenta)
meanings.note: Letra de imprenta means neat printed block letters.

examples.text: La imprenta es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The printing press is very important here.
We talk about the printing press.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Tu letra means 'your handwriting'.

examples.trans: The handwriting is here.

examples.text: Vemos las letras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the handwritings from the door.

meanings.note: Plural limones.

examples.trans: The lemon is here.

examples.text: Vemos los limones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lemons from the door.

lo.gloss: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)

meanings.en: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)
meanings.note: Direct object pronoun before verbs (lo veo), and neuter article in lo que ('what') or lo mejor ('the best').

examples.text: Ya lo veo encima del estante.
examples.trans: I see it now on the shelf.

examples.text: Lo mejor del patio es la calma.
examples.trans: The best part of the courtyard is the calm.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.
examples.trans: Cross the bridge and then turn.
See you later, have a good day!

meanings.note: Hacer la maleta = to pack one's suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en la maleta.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in the suitcase.

meanings.note: In azul marino, invariable or agreeing depending on style.

examples.trans: It is a marine piece.

examples.text: ¿Esa es la vieja maleta azul marino del taller del abuelo?
examples.trans: Is that the old dark-blue bag from Grandfather's workshop?

meanings.note: Por lo menos = at least; echar de menos = to miss; a menos que = unless.

examples.trans: It is ten to eight.

examples.text: Por lo menos ya no llueve.
examples.trans: At least it is no longer raining.

meanings.note: Tener miedo = be afraid; entrarle miedo = to panic.

examples.text: El miedo es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The fear is very important here.
We talk about the fear.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Describes a mystery caller or note.

examples.trans: It is a mysterious piece.

examples.text: Pues claro que vine. ¿Por qué te escondiste detrás de una nota misteriosa?
examples.trans: Of course I came. Why did you hide behind a mystery note?

meanings.note: De momento = for now.

examples.trans: The moment is here.

examples.text: Vemos los momentos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the moments from the door.

meanings.note: Stressed possessive (el mío, la mía, los míos, las mías); ¡Madre mía! = Goodness me!

examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

examples.text: Un amigo mío vive en esta calle.
examples.trans: A friend of mine lives on this street.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.trans: I need a pen to sign.
Do you all need another towel?

meanings.note: Covers jotted notes, musical notes, and review scores.

examples.trans: The note is here.

examples.text: Vemos las notas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notes from the door.

meanings.note: Letra ordenada = neat handwriting.

examples.trans: It is a neat piece.

examples.text: Reconocí tu letra ordenada de imprenta en esa postal en dos segundos.
examples.trans: I recognized your neat block handwriting on that postcard in two seconds.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: Describes a heavy suitcase, wrench, or coat.

examples.trans: It is a heavy piece.

examples.text: Cerrada y vaciada. Pásame la llave inglesa pesada de tu izquierda.
examples.trans: Off and drained. Pass me the heavy wrench on your left.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: One word without accent (distinct from ¿por qué? = why?).

examples.text: Abro la ventana porque hace calor.
examples.trans: I open the window because it is warm.
She smiles because it smells of cinnamon.

meanings.note: Short for tarjeta postal.

examples.trans: The postcard is here.

examples.text: Vemos las postales desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the postcards from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Pues claro! = Well of course!

examples.text: ¡Pues claro que te guardo un trozo!
examples.trans: Well of course I will save you a piece!
Well then, let us go inside right now.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

quitar.gloss: to remove; to wipe off; to take off (quitarse)

meanings.en: to remove; to wipe off; to take off (quitarse)
meanings.note: Quítate el abrigo = take off your coat; quitar el polvo = dust.

examples.text: Quito el polvo del tablero de madera.
examples.trans: I wipe the dust off the wooden board.

examples.text: Quítate el abrigo mojado y pasa.
examples.trans: Take off your wet coat and come in.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg reconozco.

examples.text: Reconozco esa canción de piano enseguida.
examples.trans: I recognize that piano song right away.

examples.text: Reconocí tu letra en el sobre.
examples.trans: I recognized your handwriting on the envelope.

saber.gloss: to know (a fact / how to); to taste (saber a)

meanings.en: to know (a fact / how to); to taste (saber a)
meanings.note: Irregular: sé, supe; sabe igual que = it tastes just like.

examples.trans: Do you know where the wrench is?

examples.text: Este bizcocho sabe a limón fresco.
examples.trans: This cake tastes of fresh lemon.

seguir.gloss: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)

meanings.en: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: sigo, sigue, siguió); seguir + gerund = keep doing.

examples.text: Sigue todo recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead to the bridge.
Is the water still hot?

meanings.note: Also a masculine noun (un segundo = one second).

examples.trans: It is a second piece.

examples.text: Segunda: Te he echado de menos estos tres años.
examples.trans: Second: I missed you these three years.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: me siento, ¡siéntese!).

examples.text: Siéntese junto a la ventana, por favor.
examples.trans: Sit down by the window, please.
We sit down under the lemon tree.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Takes el when talking about someone (el señor Martín), no article when addressing directly (¡Buenos días, señor!).

examples.trans: The sir is here.

examples.text: Vemos los señores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sirs from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: suyo, suya, suyos, suyas.

examples.trans: The courtyard is all yours.
Do not worry, it is not your fault.

meanings.note: Plural los talleres.

examples.trans: The workshop is here.

examples.text: Vemos los talleres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the workshops from the door.

meanings.note: Positive counterpart of tampoco.

examples.text: Yo también quiero un trozo de bizcocho.
examples.trans: I want a piece of sponge cake too.
We also have mint tea.

meanings.note: Object/reflexive pronoun corresponding to tú.

examples.text: Te guardo un rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I am saving a cinnamon roll for you.
What is your name?

meanings.note: Pleasantly warm (not scalding hot).

examples.trans: It is a warm piece.

examples.text: Toque el radiador: arriba está templado, pero abajo se está enfriando.
examples.trans: Touch the radiator: the top is lukewarm, yet the bottom is getting cold.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: ¿Qué tiempo hace? asks about the weather; a tiempo = on time.

examples.trans: The time is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tiempos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the times from the door.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: ¡Toma! = Here you go!; tomar un café = have a coffee.

examples.trans: What would you like to have for breakfast?
Here you go, here is the flashlight.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Ponemos tres mesas bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We set three tables under the tree.
Start with three short sentences.

meanings.note: Unaccented possessive (tu llave / tus llaves), distinct from accented pronoun tú.

examples.trans: Where is your toolbox?
I recognized your handwriting right away.

meanings.note: Accented té ('tea') distinguishes the noun from pronoun te ('you').

examples.trans: The tea is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tés desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the teas from the door.

meanings.note: Accented subject pronoun (tú mismo = you yourself).

examples.text: Tú conoces muy bien el barrio.
examples.trans: You know the neighbourhood very well.
Try it yourself.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

venir.gloss: to come (el verano que viene = next summer)

meanings.en: to come (el verano que viene = next summer)
meanings.note: Irregular: vengo, vienes, viene, vine.

examples.trans: Thank you for coming this morning.

examples.text: Nos vemos la semana que viene.
examples.trans: See you next week.

meanings.note: La verdad = honestly / the truth.

examples.trans: The truth is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verdades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the truths from the door.

meanings.note: Before a noun (un viejo amigo), means 'long-standing / dear old'.

examples.trans: It is an old piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el viernes ('on Friday'), los viernes ('on Fridays').

examples.trans: The Friday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los viernes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Fridays from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Often omitted in Spanish unless adding contrast or emphasis.

examples.text: Yo abro la puerta y tú llevas la linterna.
examples.trans: I will open the door and you carry the flashlight.
It is me, please open up.
